methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ground Control Development, a seed-stage housing and construction technology company founded by Lizzy Manzi, has raised $2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five private-stage construction-tech companies including BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, ADMARES, and Hedral. No directly comparable public companies trade in this narrow subsector, limiting benchmarking depth.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier to the company's $2M total raised as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $5M. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics from seed to post-seed rounds within frontier construction technology. Given the limited methodological reach available—only one valuation approach proved applicable with the data at hand—this single result anchors the analysis.

The triangulation range spans $4M (low) to $6M (median $5M), reflecting inherent uncertainty around comparable company multiples and the thinness of both public and private comp data in this segment. Key uncertainties include the degree to which private construction-tech peers trade at similar stage-based markups and whether Ground Control's specific technology platform and traction justify positioning within the range. Additional due diligence on revenue run rate, customer concentration, and technical differentiation would be necessary to refine this valuation further.
